variables.name: STUDYID
variables.label: Study Identifier
variables.description: Unique identifier for a study.

variables.name: DOMAIN
variables.label: Domain Abbreviation
variables.description: Two-character abbreviation for the domain.

variables.name: USUBJID
variables.label: Unique Subject Identifier
variables.description: Identifier used to uniquely identify a subject across all studies for all applications or submissions involving the product.

variables.name: VSSEQ
variables.label: Sequence Number
variables.description: Sequence number given to ensure uniqueness of subject records within a domain. May be any valid number.

variables.name: VSGRPID
variables.label: Group ID
variables.description: Used to tie together a block of related records in a single domain for a subject.

variables.name: VSSPID
variables.label: Sponsor-Defined Identifier
variables.description: Sponsor-defined reference number. May be preprinted on the CRF as an explicit line identifier or defined in the sponsor's operational database.

variables.name: VSTESTCD
variables.label: Vital Signs Test Short Name
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C66741
variables.description: Short name of the measurement, test, or examination described in VSTEST. It can be used as a column name when converting a dataset from a vertical to a horizontal format. The value in VSTESTCD cannot be longer than 8 characters, nor can it start with a number (e.g., "1TEST" is not valid). VSTESTCD cannot contain characters other than letters, numbers, or underscores. Examples: "SYSBP", "DIABP", "BMI".

variables.name: VSTEST
variables.label: Vital Signs Test Name
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C67153
variables.description: Verbatim name of the test or examination used to obtain the measurement or finding. The value in VSTEST cannot be longer than 40 characters. Examples: "Systolic Blood Pressure", "Diastolic Blood Pressure", "Body Mass Index".

variables.name: VSCAT
variables.label: Category for Vital Signs
variables.description: Used to define a category of related records.

variables.name: VSSCAT
variables.label: Subcategory for Vital Signs
variables.description: A further categorization of a measurement or examination.

variables.name: VSPOS
variables.label: Vital Signs Position of Subject
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C71148
variables.description: Position of the subject during a measurement or examination. Examples: "SUPINE", "STANDING", "SITTING".

variables.name: VSORRES
variables.label: Result or Finding in Original Units
variables.description: Result of the vital signs measurement as originally received or collected.

variables.name: VSORRESU
variables.label: Original Units
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C66770
variables.description: Original units in which the data were collected. The unit for VSORRES. Examples: "in", "LB", "beats/min".

variables.name: VSSTRESC
variables.label: Character Result/Finding in Std Format
variables.description: Contains the result value for all findings, copied or derived from VSORRES in a standard format or standard units. VSSTRESC should store all results or findings in character format; if results are numeric, they should also be stored in numeric format in VSSTRESN. For example, if a test has results "NONE", "NEG", and "NEGATIVE" in VSORRES, and these results effectively have the same meaning, they could be represented in standard format in VSSTRESC as "NEGATIVE".

variables.name: VSSTRESN
variables.label: Numeric Result/Finding in Standard Units
variables.description: Used for continuous or numeric results or findings in standard format; copied in numeric format from VSSTRESC. VSSTRESN should store all numeric test results or findings.

variables.name: VSSTRESU
variables.label: Standard Units
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C66770
variables.description: Standardized unit used for VSSTRESC and VSSTRESN.

variables.name: VSSTAT
variables.label: Completion Status
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C66789
variables.description: Used to indicate that a vital sign measurement was not done. Should be null if a result exists in VSORRES.

variables.name: VSREASND
variables.label: Reason Not Performed
variables.description: Describes why a measurement or test was not performed. Examples: "BROKEN EQUIPMENT", "SUBJECT REFUSED". Used in conjunction with VSSTAT when value is "NOT DONE".

variables.name: VSLOC
variables.label: Location of Vital Signs Measurement
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C74456
variables.description: Location relevant to the collection of vital signs measurement. Example: "ARM" for blood pressure.

variables.name: VSLAT
variables.label: Laterality
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C99073
variables.description: Qualifier for anatomical location or specimen further detailing laterality. Examples: "RIGHT", "LEFT", "BILATERAL".

variables.name: VSLOBXFL
variables.label: Last Observation Before Exposure Flag
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C66742
variables.description: Operationally derived indicator used to identify the last non-missing value prior to RFXSTDTC. Should be "Y" or null.

variables.name: VSBLFL
variables.label: Baseline Flag
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C66742
variables.description: Indicator used to identify a baseline value. Should be "Y" or null. Note that VSBLFL is retained for backward compatibility. The authoritative baseline for statistical analysis is in an ADaM dataset.

variables.name: VSDRVFL
variables.label: Derived Flag
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C66742
variables.description: Used to indicate a derived record. The value should be "Y" or null. Records that represent the average of other records or that do not come from the CRF are examples of records that would be derived for the submission datasets. If VSDRVFL = "Y," then VSORRES may be null, with VSSTRESC and (if numeric) VSSTRESN having the derived value.

variables.name: VSTOX
variables.label: Toxicity
variables.description: Description of toxicity quantified by VSTOXGR. The sponsor is expected to provide the name of the scale and version used to map the terms, utilizing the external codelist element in the Define-XML document.

variables.name: VSTOXGR
variables.label: Standard Toxicity Grade
variables.description: Records toxicity grade value using a standard toxicity scale (e.g., NCI CTCAE). If value is from a numeric scale, represent only the number (e.g., "2", not "Grade 2"). The sponsor is expected to provide the name of the scale and version used to map the terms, utilizing the external codelist element in the Define-XML document.

variables.name: VSCLSIG
variables.label: Clinically Significant, Collected
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C66742
variables.description: Used to indicate whether a collected observation is clinically significant based on judgment.

variables.name: VISITNUM
variables.label: Visit Number
variables.description: Clinical encounter number. Numeric version of VISIT, used for sorting.

variables.name: VISIT
variables.label: Visit Name
variables.description: Protocol-defined description of clinical encounter. May be used in addition to VISITNUM and/or VISITDY.

variables.name: VISITDY
variables.label: Planned Study Day of Visit
variables.description: Planned study day of the visit based upon RFSTDTC in Demographics.

variables.name: TAETORD
variables.label: Planned Order of Element within Arm
variables.description: Number that gives the planned order of the element within the arm.

variables.name: EPOCH
variables.label: Epoch
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C99079
variables.description: Epoch associated with the start date/time at which the assessment was made.

variables.name: VSDTC
variables.label: Date/Time of Measurements
variables.description: Date and time of the vital signs assessment represented in ISO 8601 character format.

variables.name: VSDY
variables.label: Study Day of Vital Signs
variables.description: Study day of vital signs measurements, measured as integer days. Algorithm for calculations must be relative to the sponsor-defined RFSTDTC variable in Demographics.

variables.name: VSTPT
variables.label: Planned Time Point Name
variables.description: Text description of time when measurement should be taken. This may be represented as an elapsed time relative to a fixed reference point (e.g., time of last dose). See VSTPTNUM and VSTPTREF. Examples: "START", "5 MIN POST".

variables.name: VSTPTNUM
variables.label: Planned Time Point Number
variables.description: Numerical version of VSTPT to aid in sorting.

variables.name: VSELTM
variables.label: Planned Elapsed Time from Time Point Ref
variables.description: Planned elapsed time (in ISO 8601) relative to a planned fixed reference (VSTPTREF). This variable is useful where there are repetitive measures. Not a clock time or a date time variable. Represented as an ISO 8601 Duration. Examples: "-PT15M" to represent the period of 15 minutes prior to the reference point indicated by VSTPTREF, "PT8H" to represent the period of 8 hours after the reference point indicated by VSTPTREF.

variables.name: VSTPTREF
variables.label: Time Point Reference
variables.description: Name of the fixed reference point referred to by VSELTM, VSTPTNUM, and VSTPT. Examples: "PREVIOUS DOSE", "PREVIOUS MEAL".

variables.name: VSRFTDTC
variables.label: Date/Time of Reference Time Point
variables.description: Date/time of the reference time point, VSTPTREF.
